answer.evidence: The water column is drawn in pure front elevation. The top dome/cap is rendered straight-on in silhouette with an arched top and flat bottom, showing no foreshortened top surface or cut face seen from a 3/4 perspective.

The dome cap atop the pillar shows a visible top surface across rows 6–10 (approx. 5 source pixel rows) before transitioning to the undercut shadow. The flared base plinth also clearly displays a foreshortened upper slope across rows 40–42.

The water crane is drawn in pure front elevation: the top cap (rows 6-12), horizontal arm, and base (rows 39-44) terminate in flat horizontal lines rather than showing foreshortened elliptical top surfaces seen from a 3/4 overhead perspective.

answer.main_body: locomotive water column (vertical iron post with top cap and horizontal crane arm)
answer.evidence: The main body is drawn in pure front elevation: the top cap (rows 6-11) is a flat silhouette dome with no visible foreshortened top surface, and the horizontal crane arm (rows 12-14) is drawn straight-on without any visible top face. Although the valve handle (rows 25-28) is drawn as an ellipse, minor details cannot substitute for the main body.
